entities.summary:
Master Hugo was a Romanesque lay artist and the earliest recorded professional artist in England. Born in unknown year, Master Hugo worked primarily in Northern Europe during the 12th century. His art, including frescoes and tapestries, can be found in various monasteries and churches across the region. The exact date of his death remains unknown.

Master Hugo's significance lies in his pioneering role in the development of medieval art in England. His work influenced subsequent generations of artists, including those of the Gothic style. The artist's exact birth and death dates are still a topic of scholarly debate.

Master Hugo's artistic legacy extends beyond his own work, as his innovations in technique and style paved the way for the development of English medieval art. His impact can still be seen in many of the region's most famous artworks.

The master's artistic output is characterized by its beauty, precision, and attention to detail, as seen in his frescoes in the Monastery of St. Albans.

This artist's impact on the course of art history is undeniable, as his work continues to inspire artists and art historians to this day.
